title: PG-09.1 Identity, admission and ACFA boundary (memev)
request: Programme contract for work package WP09 in memev: Identity, admission and ACFA boundary. Proposed and unsigned; the signer signs it after the red-team gate. Source: the programme decomposition of 31 Oct 2026 (docs/scope-one/programme/WBS.md, docs/scope-one/programme/DECOMPOSITION.md, docs/scope-one/programme/fragments/WP09.json) and the owner notes behind docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md. Depends on tasks outside this contract: WP04-02, WP06-02. Covers only what the Scope One contracts (SO-1.01 to SO-1.11) do not already cover; the mapping is in contracts/programme/manifest.json. Boundary with SO-2.12: WP09-02 (the contribution-admission boundary) is a prerequisite of federated computation and is not repeated there. Signed vault contract MEM-145, MEM-146 and MEM-147 (cited by id only): foundation: human binding of agent roles; WP09-01 reuses it. Signed vault contract WO-05-D (cited by id only): the external trust service specification; the adapters of WP09-02 and WP09-03 sit on its boundary and this spec does not specify the service. Build layer (owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026): the signed fold contracts SO-F-01, SO-F-03, SO-F-08 (cited by id; delivered by pull request #341, WBS.md section 9.2 on its branch) are the build layer. Each task below that overlaps them cites the fold id and keeps only what the fold does not cover. Tasks of this spec that name no fold contract have no fold overlap. Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository and is reached only across the WO-05-A call-out boundary (never vendored, no memev-merge); tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that; there is no Federated tier.

tasks.description: Repo: memev. Keeps only the admission of a node or agent to a site. Subjects, keys, expiry, revocation, scope types and request resolution are SO-F-01; a contribution signature and its two-step admission are SO-F-03; the role bindings are MEM-145, MEM-146 and MEM-147 (cited by id). This task builds on them and defines no subject, key scheme, token or contribution check. A site node is a subject of type node, as SO-F-01 defines it (this task and WP13-03 were one duplicate; WP13-03 reuses this).

tasks.title: Equivocation and suspicious-contribution handler: evidence goes to Memev authority and exclusion policy
requirements: MV-TRU-07: Equivocation and suspicious contributions are detected and handed to Memev authority and exclusion policy. (source: owner notes of 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md:56; evidence docs/scope-one/programme/DECOMPOSITION.md:99; baseline 8.5)

Equivocation and admission invariants: the key is convicted, not the message; the trust anchor comes from outside the artefact; duplicates are removed on semantic identity, not signature bytes; an identity with two entries in one round is excluded entirely at admission; validity is evaluated at read time; trust signals track conduct, not distance from consensus (source: converge src/receipts.py and tests/test_receipts.py, described only, itself a port of the acfa-rs accountability core; repository analysis of 1 Nov 2026, section 3.4 item C2)
